front: When is a subsidiary consolidated (voting interest model)?
back: When the parent has a **controlling financial interest** — generally **> 50%** of voting shares.

front: What percentage of intercompany transactions is eliminated?
back: **100%**, regardless of the parent's ownership percentage.
Intercompany gross profit × portion of the goods **still held** by the buying affiliate at year-end.

front: Markup on cost → profit in ending inventory
back: Profit = transfer price − (transfer price ÷ (1 + markup %)). E.g., 25% on cost: profit = 20% of transfer price.
Eliminate the gain; restore original cost & accumulated depreciation; remove **excess depreciation** each year (realizing the gain over the life).

front: Upstream vs. downstream sale — why it matters
back: **Upstream** (sub → parent): unrealized profit reduces the **sub's** income, so it affects the NCI share. Downstream (parent → sub): it's the parent's profit.
In **equity**, separately from parent equity; consolidated net income is **attributed** to parent and NCI on the face of the income statement.
